question.text: Based on the knowledge about deicing operations learned from the conversation, what is the main reason for flight delays during heavy snow conditions?

questions.original_answer: 1) Icy runways prevent aircraft from taking off and landing safely (due to increased braking distance); 2) Ice accumulation on the wings affects the aircraft's lift, posing a threat to flight safety; 3) De-icing operations themselves are time-consuming, requiring 20-30 minutes per aircraft, and long queues of flights can lead to significant delays.

supporting_evidence.content: Dawei: Blizzard warning, temperature -31 degrees, flights might indeed be delayed.
Dawei: [Send picture: img5.jpg] Look at this weather forecast, there's a blizzard warning, flights might be delayed.
Dawei: @Old Zhang, the snow is so heavy that it's doubtful whether the plane can take off. A delay is probably unavoidable.

Dawei: In this kind of blizzard weather, planes have to undergo de-icing operations before takeoff. If the runway is icy, the plane can't brake properly; if the wings are icy, it affects lift. De-icing a single plane takes about 20 to 30 minutes, and with so many planes in line, we'll definitely have to wait a long time.
Dawei: [Sending picture: img12.jpg] Everyone, look at the blizzard outside the window. The snow is so heavy that it's even questionable whether planes can take off.
